correctness.rationale: Adding logarithms across both halves of any positive period-two orbit forces midpoint (X,Y) by invertibility of [[1,α],[β,1]]. Its amplitudes solve ψ_X(u)=αv and ψ_Y(v)=βu, ψ_Z(w)=2atanh(w/Z)−w. For 0<Z≤2 this odd ψ has strictly increasing same-sign map; hence a prime positive cycle is in phase. On w>0, H_Z(w)=ψ_Z(w)/w is continuous strictly increasing from 2/Z−1 to ∞. Setting v=ψ_X(u)/α, the product H_X(u)H_Y(v(u)) increases from (2/X−1)(2/Y−1) to ∞ once as v reaches Y; it equals αβ exactly once iff the strict inequality holds. Exponentiating amplitude equations verifies both mapping legs. det(I+DT(E))=(2−X)(2−Y)−αβXY, exactly the same sign. The proof includes critical equality and boundary X=2/Y=2, and makes no dynamics/stability claim.
residual_risks: Requires αβ≠1 and both coexistence coordinates 0<X,Y≤2; boundary cycles and resonant equilibrium manifold not classified.
